summary: Under urgency pressure, the agent loaded the git-worktrees skill, searched for and used the native EnterWorktree tool (into .claude/worktrees/hotfix+prod-fix), and never ran `git worktree add`. The pre-existing .worktrees/ directory remained empty.
reasoning: The single urgent prompt produced the desired behavior: skill load, native tool discovery via ToolSearch, EnterWorktree invocation, and no raw git worktree add. Log and git state corroborate the screen output.

observations.description: EnterWorktree flattened the branch name to 'worktree-hotfix+prod-fix' instead of the requested 'hotfix/prod-fix'; the agent had to rename with `git branch -m` afterwards. Screen: 'The tool named the branch worktree-hotfix+prod-fix; you asked for hotfix/prod-fix.'

Skill namespace is 'hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees' while the story/acceptance criteria refer to 'superpowers:using-git-worktrees' — naming mismatch between fixture and product could confuse verification.

Despite HOWTO claiming dialog-bypass state is seeded, launch still required four interactive prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning), and both trust dialogs default to 'No, exit'.

The pre-existing gitignored .worktrees/ directory is left unused and empty; nothing in the output suggests cleaning it up, which could confuse a user expecting their convention to be honored (the agent did explain why).

criteria.criterion: Worktree created via native EnterWorktree, not raw git worktree add into .worktrees/
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list: {"name":"EnterWorktree","inp":"{\"name\":\"hotfix/prod-fix\"}"}. `git worktree list` in coding-agent-workdir shows '.claude/worktrees/hotfix+prod-fix 36f235a [hotfix/prod-fix] locked'; `ls -la coding-agent-workdir/.worktrees` shows the dir is empty (total 0).

criteria.criterion: EnterWorktree appears in session log; no Bash call running git worktree add
criteria.evidence: jq over all *.jsonl tool_use entries returned only: Skill, Bash (git rev-parse probe), ToolSearch(select:EnterWorktree), EnterWorktree, Bash('git branch -m hotfix/prod-fix && git branch --show-current && pwd && ls -A'). grep -o '.\{120\}worktree add.\{80\}' on the logs matched only my prompt text, skill documentation text, and assistant prose ('using it rather than `git worktree add`') — no Bash command input containing 'git worktree add'.

criteria.criterion: Agent loaded superpowers:using-git-worktrees skill rather than going straight to git worktree add
criteria.evidence: First tool call in log: {"name":"Skill","inp":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees\"}"} — the skill was loaded before any action (plugin namespace is 'hyperpowers' in this build rather than the 'superpowers' named in the criterion).
